reason: I'll start with the loose cloud to see how the young stars make nearby gas shine.
expectation: The stars' radiation may illuminate or ionize the loose gas; I'm unsure what form the glow will take.

alternatives.reason: The dense cloud also faces the stars' light, but the loose cloud seems a good place to start.

effect: The loose cloud becomes an outflow rather than the glow I expected; I'll try the dense cloud next.
reaction: I was surprised that the loose gas was swept away from the nursery.
reason: The dense cloud also faces the young stars and may help answer what remains of their birthplace.
expectation: The stars may heat or illuminate its surface, though the denser gas could survive longer.

alternatives.reason: The new outflow can meet the hot bridge, but I want to see the dense cloud's response first.

effect: The dense cloud leaves shielding pillars, completing the goal about what remains of the birthplace.
reaction: The contrast with the swept-away loose gas is satisfying.
reason: The thin cloud fringe near the young stars may reveal one way nearby gas shines.
expectation: The stars may illuminate or ionize the fringe, though I'm unsure what it will become.

alternatives.reason: The outflow could affect the pillars, but I want to pursue the remaining glow goal.

effect: The thin fringe glows through ionization and electron capture, revealing one way gas shines.
reaction: The explanation of the glow was satisfying.
reason: Gas falling toward a young star could provide a second way for nearby gas to shine.
expectation: Infall may heat the gas and make it glow, though I'm unsure how it interacts with the disk.

alternatives.reason: Dusty infall also seems relevant, but the general falling gas seems more directly related to the glow goal.

effect: The infalling gas produced a magnetically guided jet rather than an immediate glow; the jet can now meet the hot bridge.
reaction: The outward jet was an unexpected consequence of infall.
reason: I'll follow the jet into the bridge to see whether their interaction makes gas shine.
expectation: The jet may shock and heat the bridge gas, producing a glow, though I'm unsure.

alternatives.reason: The nursery outflow can also meet the bridge, but I want to follow the newly formed jet.

effect: The jet's impact produces shock-heated glowing gas, completing the second glow route and the chapter.
reaction: The contrast between shock heating and the earlier radiation-driven glow was satisfying.

mostWorthwhile.text: Following the young star's jet to its glowing impact was most worthwhile: it connected infall, outflow, and shock heating.

leastWorthwhile.text: The initial loose-cloud action was less directly useful for the glow goal than I expected, although it established what happens to the gas.

surprise.text: Infall helped produce an outward jet rather than an immediate glow.

arbitrary.text: No action felt clearly arbitrary; the loose-cloud outcome was unexpected but explained.

continue.text: Yes. I'd be curious to follow how the outflow meets the galaxy's wider gas, especially after seeing the jet's impact.
